STI prevalence among HIV-infected women in South Africa is high and that the burden of asymptomatic infections is substantial, thus justifying the use of diagnostic STI screening rather than syndromes-based approaches.

STI screening of HIV-infected women in antenatal settings in low income settings is warranted to prevent mother-to-child transmission of STIs and to reduce the risk of adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes.
